newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's biggest newspaper endorses ruling Liberals.
newsitem.headline: Canada's biggest newspaper endorses ruling Liberals.

text.p: Canada's most widely read newspaper endorsed the ruling Liberal Party for re-election in an editorial on Saturday, just eight days before the polling.
The left-leaning Toronto Star newspaper urged Canadians to give the Liberals a second majority government when they go to the polls for the nation's 36th federal election on June 2.
The editorial, headlined "Liberals Deserve a Second Majority," said only the Liberals "have the team, the record and the policies to lead Canada into the 21st century."

It said the Liberals, who are ahead in the polls, have managed the economy well through "painful but necessary belt-tightening" which has begun to show dividends in an improved economy, rising consumer confidence and the decline of the federal deficit.

"They have managed the economy well. They reflect the values of fairness and social responsibility we cherish, And they have strength in every region of the country to draw on, as Canada faces another showdown with Quebec's separatist forces," the Star told its 2.2 million Saturday readers.

The Star praised the Progressive Conservative Leader Jean Charest for his leadership in the national debate over unity with the French-speaking province of Quebec. But it said his party has not fully recovered from its shattering election defeat in 1993, which threw the Conservatives from a governing majority to only two seats in the nation's 295-seat parliament.

The Star castigated the right-wing, western-based Reform Party Leader Preston Manning for pandering to "anti-Quebec sentiment" after Manning's party began airing television advertisments that suggested Quebec-born politicians did not have what it takes to keep Quebec from leaving Canada.
